text:
Samir: Overnight handoff — quick summary of what happened and what's needed for the next shift. TL;DR: embeddings-service started returning 503s intermittently ~02:10-02:40 UTC, pagers fired, we routed a subset to small-model fallback and stabilized traffic. Primary handled the initial pages. Current status: degraded but passing traffic via fallback, autoscaler recovering. See actions and playbook below.

Incident Bot: ALERT: pager triggered for embeddings-service (svc-embeddings-prod) — 503 rate increased above threshold (5m p95). Pager TS: 4470012300.

Samir: Timeline: 02:08 alert, 02:10 spike to 18% 503, 02:14 mitigation: enabled traffic-shed -> fallback-model, 02:20 scaled worker pool + bumped replica count, 02:33 KV-cache warmed, 02:40 error rate down to ~0.8%. Root cause: suspected upstream congestion on a subset of GPU host group (gpu-pool-eu-3) causing long tail and request queue exhaustion. Still investigating hardware telemetry.

Maria: Customer impact: small bucket of customers (IDs in support ticket #CS-8893) saw failed embedding requests for ~15–30s windows. No broad SLA breaches but some retries visible in logs. I raised a support note and pinged account leads.

Kevin: Playbook steps executed: enabled fallback routing policy (route->fallback-small), scaled embedding-worker deployment. Commands used:
```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deploy embedding-worker --replicas=10
# confirm pods coming up
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=embedding-worker -o wide
```
Also applied temporary circuit-breaker to upstream GPU pool:
```yaml
# partial snippet applied via rollout policy
- name: gpu-pool-eu-3
  max_inflight: 120
  retry: 1
```
This prevented long-queue tail from backing up front-end proxies.

Priya: Observability notes: spike correlated with a batch job from partner svc-batcher-eu that ran at 02:05. We're throttling that job for now and asked infra to review windowed batch sizing. Traces show KV cache misses rising concurrently; warming reduced those misses.

Runbook Bot: Reference runbook: https://redwood.company/runbooks/embeddings-503-mitigation (runbook id: RB-2026-emb-03). Follow sections A (triage), B (fallback enable), C (scale + circuit-breaker), D (customer comms).

Samir: Action items for incoming shift (assignments):
- Primary: Maria (monitor errors, own customer comms) @maria
- Secondary: Kevin (infra scaling follow-ups, ensure replica health) @kevin
- Oncall SRE: Priya (look into batch job throttling and KV cache patterns) @priya
- Keep Incident Bot alerting for 5m p95 > 1% and escalate if > 3% for 10m.

Maria: Quick checklist for handoff:
- Verify fallback routing still active and functioning.
- Watch p50/p95 latency for fallback model; ensure quality SLAs for affected customers.
- Post a short note to #customer-impact if CS sees follow-ups.

Kevin: Notes for next steps if it flares again:
1) Temporarily block svc-batcher-eu via policy if not responding to throttles.
2) Increase embedding-worker replicas to 15 (manual) and monitor CPU/GPU queue lengths.
3) If GPU host group is unhealthy, failover traffic to secondary pool (gpu-pool-us-1) using routing policy 'route-by-health'.

Priya: Logs I saved (snippet):
```
[02:12:14] svc-embeddings prod 503 request_id=abc123 host=gpu-node-17 queue_len=98
[02:12:15] svc-embeddings prod 503 request_id=abc124 host=gpu-node-17 queue_len=102
[02:18:01] svc-embeddings prod 200 request_id=abc150 host=gpu-node-08 queue_len=4
```
Saved to /var/log/oncall/4470012345-emb-503.log

Samir: Current status: fallback routing active, replica count at 10, KV-cache warming done, partner batch job throttled. Next shift please: keep an eye on host health metrics (queue_len, GPU util, p95 tail). We've opened infra ticket #INF-6721 to review host group saturation and hardware telemetry.

Maria: I'm on for primary. I'll post a customer-impact summary if CS confirms new support hits.

Kevin: I'll follow infra ticket and be ready to run failover if needed. I've left the kubectl commands in the runbook but pasted critical ones in thread.

Incident Bot: RESOLVED ALERT: embeddings-service 503 rate returned below threshold at 4470013750. Monitoring remains active.

Samir: Closing notes: if you need the exact routing policy ID it's rp-emb-fb-12. If anyone takes an action, drop a short one-line confirmation here (e.g., 'Kevin: scaled to 12'). Thanks — handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
